rendered: The document does not describe choosing copper for the anode-free cell. Its anode-free cell is built on aluminum: carbon films are assembled on Al foil, and the carbon/Al electrode serves as the current collector. The authors explain the choice of Al over Cu directly: Al was selected instead of[1] Cu because it offers significant cost (∼3× cheaper) and weight[2] (∼3× lighter) benefits[3], a advantage they tie to transitioning to sodium-based chemistries. Copper appears in the paper only in a comparison with prior work, where using Cu electrodes reported nearly double the hysteresis at[4] in the authors' comparison (Figure S4).
